findings.text: The loop removes the match with an unquoted `${output//${BASH_REMATCH[0]}/}`, so the glob treats `[31m` as a bracket class instead of literal text. Output containing `\033[31m` never gets stripped, the `=~` test stays true, and the `while` loop never ends, hanging the formatter.

The old code escaped every ESC byte, and the new code only strips `ESC[digits;m` color sequences. Other escapes such as `\033[K`, `\033[2J`, `\033[1;32;mX` or a bare ESC now pass through as raw 0x1B bytes, which makes the JUnit XML invalid.
The regex needs at least one character (`[0-9;]+`), so the bare reset sequence `\033[m` is not stripped. With the glob bug fixed, it would still leave a stray `ESC[m` in the output.

0.reason: The regex only matches ESC, '[', digits, ';' and 'm', so the matched text never contains a closing ']'. Bash treats an unclosed '[' in a pattern as a literal character, so the unquoted substitution does remove the sequence and the loop ends.
